      "content": "# Frozen Phase A — modular native square-distance ambiguity

Candidate-ID: FREE-X6-MODSQ-C69018-20261015.
Researcher-ID: EM-FREE-C69018.
Mode: direct FREE_AXIOM_DISCOVERY; no Task or claim.
Local substrate checkout: 7317568f2eca4aa89fa2f22266f390e5f07b6b5d.
Knowledge bootstrap reported by parent: 14cb7de3fcfbd412755906faefc8e038fd5fbce6; not a newly performed verification by this researcher.

## Origin and blindness

The primitive substrate supplies an affine Z^6 Cell torsor, the squared six-component displacement readout, and the obligation to retain distinctions relevant to declared future observations. I independently ask what exact location ambiguity remains when all such square-distance readings are recorded modulo one integer. This asks a finite-resolution question about all six spatial coordinates; it introduces no native plane or lower-dimensional starting world.

Blindness status is ANCHOR_EXPOSED, never CLEAN. Before this freeze I read mandatory AGENTS and substrate files, including the current all-research Weighted-BRC substrate (which actually contains downstream commitment names and tool IDs), and the entire X6 torsor definition (which actually contains existing coordinate/path results and a short open-questions section). I did not use those sections as a candidate menu. I read no general current-result router, task/result/review directory, task agenda, detailed tool registry or prior research note. The actual exposure ledger is a separate file; its hashes bind the bytes available at freeze. The original parent message is also exposure, but supplied no mathematical topic.

## Exact question and semantic layer

Fix a Cell anchor c and six signed primitive positive displacements e_1,...,e_6. A Cell x has raw signed chart z in Z^6. These are proof coordinates, not final public addresses. Write q(z)=sum_{i=1}^6 z_i^2, the existing native component square readout; it does not import Euclidean native angles.

For every integer m>=1, first take the declared residue observer z bar in V_m=(Z/mZ)^6. All residue vectors are retained, with no prime-only, odd-only or coprimality filtering. Let A={0,e_1,...,e_6} and define F_m(z bar)=(q(z-a) mod m)_{a in A}. Compare it with the infinite family U_m(z bar)=(q(z-a) mod m)_{a in Z^6}. The family index a is retained jointly, not replaced by unassociated marginals.

The question: determine the exact common fibers of F_m and U_m; determine when the residue position is recoverable; and prove whether their quotient is safe for the declared language of arbitrary common integer translations and all future modular square-distance queries.

This is a static spatial observer question. Future translations here mean allowed algebraic compositions, not a physical evolution law or a calibrated time sequence. No dynamics or seventh spatial coordinate is introduced. If an actual time-indexed process is added, time must be separately typed.

## Candidate statement

The two observers have identical fibers, and each fiber is a coset of the following subgroup K_m of V_m:

1. If m is odd (including m=1), K_m={0}, so the readout recovers the full residue position.
2. If m=2s with s odd, K_m={s epsilon : epsilon in {0,1}^6, sum epsilon_i even}. Each fiber has 32 points.
3. If 4 divides m, K_m={(m/2) epsilon : epsilon in {0,1}^6}. Each fiber has 64 points.

No modulus m makes this a lossless encoding of an unrestricted full Cell: z and z+m e_i always have the same residue observations. The odd-modulus injectivity statement concerns only V_m. Each quotient is stable under every common integer translation; every future observation q(z+t-a) mod m factors through it. This safety lease excludes exact Cell equality, finer-modulus reads, parity-labelled coordinates not already determined, direct raw-coordinate access, path provenance, channel/branch decorations, and independent operations on forgotten relational records.

## Derivation idea, consequences, falsifiers

Subtract the anchor-0 reading from the anchor-e_i reading: q(z-e_i)-q(z)=1-2z_i. Thus equality of F_m implies 2(z'_i-z_i)=0 mod m and q(z')=q(z) mod m, which also suffice for equality of every anchor reading. With delta=z'-z, use q(z+delta)-q(z)=2 z dot delta+q(delta). The first term vanishes modulo m once 2delta=0. For odd m, delta=0. For even m=2s, delta=s epsilon, so q(delta)=s^2 sum epsilon_i. This vanishes modulo 2s for exactly even-weight epsilon when s is odd, and for every epsilon when s is even. Translation adds 2t dot delta, which vanishes as well. These arguments are candidates for a complete paper proof after the mandatory coverage gate.

Immediate consequence: arbitrarily many modular square-distance landmarks cannot repair the even-modulus hidden residue subgroup. A different typed observation would be required if the declared language needs those distinctions.

Obvious falsifiers: any even-m fiber difference with 2delta nonzero; any epsilon of odd weight in an m=2 mod 4 fiber; any m divisible by 4 where one of the 64 half-modulus shifts changes a reading; any future common translation that separates an asserted fiber. A scope failure is also a falsifier of an overbroad claim: exact Cell or finer-modulus queries are deliberately excluded.

## Bound and status

At most one bounded derivation unit: this exact fiber theorem and its translation-safe scope. No numerical search is planned or needed, no new general-purpose mechanism/tool is proposed, and no novelty or axiom status is claimed. Phase B must first look up current coverage, reuse, and directly related evidence; coverage may require CONSUME/COMPOSE or RESULT_ONLY. This candidate is derived algebra, not a replacement for P000 and not Working Truth or Native acceptance.
